summary: Plan, test and assess responsible tourism ventures with practical demand, finance and impact exercises. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Environmental and tourism entrepreneurship assesses whether visitor ventures can be viable while accounting for ecological limits and local value. For tourism venture founders, destination advisers and environmental project leads, the training develops practical ways to screen sites, test customer demand and shape a business model around seasonal costs and local suppliers. Participants also practise setting visitor-use thresholds, reviewing nature-related safeguards, estimating seasonal break-even points and defining environmental and local-benefit indicators.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape, assess or support tourism ventures with environmental and local economic goals. It suits people who need to test demand, plan viable operations or present a credible venture case.
modules: Tourism Site Feasibility and Limits of Acceptable Change
Tourism Venture Unit Economics with Excel
Tourism Venture Pitch and Theory of Change
prerequisites: Working familiarity with tourism operations, environmental projects or small-business planning is recommended. No coding or specialist software is required; exercises use case information and worksheets.
